verses.text: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
All the king’s servants who were in the king’s gate bowed down, and paid homage to Haman; for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai didn’t bow down or pay him homage.
Then the king’s servants, who were in the king’s gate, said to Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the king’s commandment?”
Now it came to pass, when they spoke daily to him, and he didn’t listen to them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s reason would stand; for he had told them that he was a Jew.
When Haman saw that Mordecai didn’t bow down, nor pay him homage, Haman was full of wrath.

But he scorned the thought of laying hands on Mordecai alone, for they had made known to him Mordecai’s people. Therefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even Mordecai’s people.

In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, and chose the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.

Haman said to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom, and their laws are different than other people’s. They don’t keep the king’s laws. Therefore it is not for the king’s profit to allow them to remain.

If it pleases the king, let it be written that they be destroyed; and I will pay ten thousand talents  of silver into the hands of those who are in charge of the king’s business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”
The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
The king said to Haman, “The silver is given to you, the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you.”

Then the king’s scribes were called in on the first month, on the thirteenth day of the month; and all that Haman commanded was written to the king’s satraps, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus, and it was sealed with the king’s ring.

Letters were sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that they should be ready against that day.
The couriers went out in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Shushan was perplexed.

footnotes.content: Haman's promotion marks a turning point—not by accident, but by the invisible hand of God arranging the board. When we see ambition rise around us, remember: the Lord is never surprised.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mordecai's refusal to bow wasn't stubborn defiance—it was faith. Some convictions cost us everything, yet they cost us nothing if they keep us tethered to what's true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servants' question reveals an old temptation: *Why don't you just go along?* Most people obey without asking. Mordecai's silence to their pressure was more faithful than any words could be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They kept asking. Day after day, the pressure mounted. Yet Mordecai's "no" never wavered. Standing alone grows easier when you're standing on something solid.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Haman's wrath burned hot—not because of a gesture, but because his pride met an immovable wall. How often our anger reveals what we've made into an idol.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wounded pride became genocide. One man's refusal to bow sparked a plot to destroy a whole people. Evil often begins small—a bruised ego—then metastasizes into horror.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The casting of lots—*Pur*—chose Adar. This word gives the book *Purim* its name. But these dice were never rolled by chance; God's hand was already turning them. The lot's answer is the Lord's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Haman's accusation rings with bitter half-truths: *They keep different laws.* Yes—God's law. The world has always condemned faithfulness as disloyalty. It's the oldest lie.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten thousand talents of silver—an absurd fortune offered to destroy a people Haman pretended to despise. His real god was malice. Money was just the proof.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king's ring—a symbol of absolute authority. Haman received it without question, and Ahasuerus sealed the fate of thousands. Power given to the wrong hands is how the world's darkness grows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The silver is yours, the people are yours"—spoken as casually as a man might hand over a cup of wine. But God knows the names of every person in Haman's shadow, and He sees them still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The decree was written and sealed, carried to every province in every language. In that moment, the machinery of empire ground forward to crush the Jews—and God had already positioned a young queen in the palace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Young and old, women and children—no mercy in the target. But the Lord loves those the world marks for destruction. Haman's cruelty revealed his blindness: he could not see the God who stood invisibly beside His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The copy of the decree spread to every people. Darkness seemed complete. And in this hour of apparent abandonment, God's purpose was already unfolding. He is faithful even when His hand is hidden.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king and Haman sat to drink while the city was perplexed. Readers today hear an echo: men celebrate premature victory before the story is over. We celebrate, too, sometimes forgetting that God writes the ending.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
